required.quote: evidence of the podiatrist's maintenance of professional medical competence, which may include continuing podiatric medical education, postgraduate studies, institutes, seminars, lectures, conferences, work shops, professional evaluation, and specialty board certification or recertification during the preceding four (4) years

available.quote: The board may issue a license to an applicant who pays a fee established by the board and who presents satisfactory evidence to the board that the applicant: (1) meets the requirements under IC 25-29-3-1; (2) is licensed in a state, territory, or possession of the United States; (3) has passed a podiatric medical licensing examination that is substantially equivalent to the examination approved by the board; and (4) has practiced podiatric medicine for at least five (5) years.

requirements.value: Must meet standard licensure requirements, be licensed in another US jurisdiction, have passed a substantially equivalent exam, and have practiced for at least 5 years. Board may require personal appearance or a new medical exam if 10+ years have elapsed since passing the licensing exam.

title_protection.quote: "Podiatrist" means an individual who: (1) practices podiatric medicine; and (2) uses one (1) or more of the following designations: (A) Doctor of podiatric medicine. (B) Podiatric physician. (C) Podiatric surgeon.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Permitting or authorizing a person to fill or refill a prescription or drug order for a legend drug except as authorized by law
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A podiatrist licensed in Indiana who permits or authorizes a person to fill or refill a prescription or drug order for a legend drug except as authorized in IC 16-42-19 is subject to disciplinary action under IC 25-1-9.

definition_quote.value: "Podiatric medicine" means the diagnosis or medical, surgical (as described in IC 25-22.5-1-1.1(a)(1)(C)), and mechanical treatment of the human foot and related structures.
definition_quote.quote: "Podiatric medicine" means the diagnosis or medical, surgical (as described in IC 25-22.5-1-1.1 (a)(1)(C)), and mechanical treatment of the human foot and related structures.

methods_authorized.quote: the diagnosis or medical, surgical (as described in IC 25-22.5-1-1.1 (a)(1)(C)), and mechanical treatment of the human foot and related structures. (b) Podiatric medicine includes the administration of local anesthetics.

drug_authority.value: Podiatrists may administer local anesthetics; they may prescribe medications as the scope of practice implies but may not authorize persons to fill or refill prescriptions for legend drugs except as authorized by IC 16-42-19.
drug_authority.quote: Podiatric medicine includes the administration of local anesthetics.

anatomical_scope_upper_boundary.quote: "Podiatric medicine" means the diagnosis or medical, surgical (as described in IC 25-22.5-1-1.1 (a)(1)(C)), and mechanical treatment of the human foot and related structures.

amputation_authorized.quote: The term does not include the amputation of the entire foot, but does include the amputation of an entire toe if the amputation is performed at an institution: (1) that is approved by a joint commission of accredited hospital organizations; and (2) where comanagement of the patient is being performed by a physician licensed under IC 25-22.5.

anesthesia_authority.quote: Podiatric medicine includes the administration of local anesthetics.

podiatric_assistant_authorized.quote: An employee of a podiatrist or group of podiatrists who performs an act, a duty, or a function that is customarily within the specific area of practice of the employing podiatrist or group of podiatrists, if the act, duty, or function is performed under the direction and supervision of the employing podiatrist

podiatric_assistant_supervision_level.quote: performed under the direction and supervision of the employing podiatrist or a podiatrist of the employing group within whose area of practice the act, duty, or function falls

impaired_practitioner_program.quote: Approve certain voluntary treatment programs for impaired podiatrists that are medically directed and nonprofit. The rules must allow an approved treatment program to be exempt from reporting to the board if the impaired podiatrist is participating satisfactorily in the program.
